key_insight: HISPO improves reinforcement learning for math reasoning by assigning credit at an intermediate segment level, bridging token-level and sequence-level policy optimization.
engineering_relevance: For long-form reasoning models, segment-level importance sampling offers a practical way to reduce credit-assignment noise and improve benchmark performance without changing the base model architecture.
method: Build contiguous response segments using rollout-time entropy signals.
Assign soft saliency weights from segment entropy.
Apply clipped importance-sampling correction at the segment granularity.
evidence_signal: The paper fine-tunes Qwen3-1.7B-Base on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks and reports stronger Pass@8 on all six and improved Acc@8 on five, including gains on AIME25 over GRPO and GSPO.
watch_item: Entropy-based segmentation and segment-level clipping may add implementation complexity and require careful tuning to avoid unstable credit assignment or over-fragmented segments.
paper_title: HISPO: Hierarchical Importance-Sampling Policy Optimization with Entropy-Derived Segments
